chunks: From him, from Fadala, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah ibn Sulayman, who said:
I asked him about buying the Mushaf (copies of the Quran), so he said: 'When you intend to buy, say: I buy from you its paper, its leather (cover), and the work of your hand for such and such.'

key_terms.الْمَصَاحِفِ: Copies of the Quran (plural of Mushaf)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication when buying a Quran?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines a specific commercial supplication for purchasing a Mushaf, emphasizing the sanctity of the Quranic text by acknowledging its physical components (paper and cover) and the scribe's labor. In Shia jurisprudence, this practice reflects the principle of *Istihbab* (commendability) in treating the Quran with reverence during transactions, distinguishing it from mundane trade. It highlights the holistic value placed on the Quran as both a divine word and a physical object worthy of respectful handling.
